title: Startup of the bridging machine
statement: For every program $c$ in the partial-recursive language and every Boolean word $x$, the four-work-tape bridging machine associated with $c$, started on the input obtained by embedding each bit of $x$ in the Boolean part of its alphabet, reaches after finitely many steps the configuration with input-head position $0$, empty output, and stack assignment holding the stack word of $x$ on the main stack and empty words on the other three stacks. Its control state is the execution state for the translated initial statement of $c$'s compilation, paired with its membership in the finite statement support, and the register is empty.
hypotheses_covered: A program c in the partial-recursive language
replaced:
From its initial configuration on the embedded Boolean input $x$, the bridging
machine of a partial-recursive program $c$ reaches the bridge configuration at input
position $0$ whose main stack holds the full stack word of $x$ (other stacks empty,
empty output), in the execution state at the translated initial statement of $c$'s
compilation, with empty register.
